clue.text: Preservative Odysseus initially used thus in a Greek island

indicators.note: in tells us the island's name is opened up to take the other pieces

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the hero's name

parts.note: thus means so, in that way

explanation.surface: Odysseus is said to have treated something with a preservative on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is only a link; the surface tempts you to read Odysseus as using a preservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a tar-based oil painted on wood to stop it rotting, a classic preservative.

clue.text: A crime novel about pot

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the words are put in a fresh order

parts.note: c is circa, Latin for about, used before dates

explanation.surface: A crime novel centres on a stash of cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges A CRIME as CERAMI, then C for 'about'. 'Crime novel' looks like a genre, and 'pot' like cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic means pottery: a pot made of fired clay is a ceramic.

clue.text: We take it in protest — it does no: follow the rule

definitions.meaning: to take offence or object is to 'take ...' to something

definitions.text: it does no: follow the rule
definitions.meaning: a case that does not obey a general rule

explanation.definitionFit: To take exception is to object, and an exception is a case outside the general rule.

clue.text: Dawn revolt given newspaper heading

indicators.note: heading tells us the newspaper goes at the top of this down entry

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a rising or rise is a revolt against rulers

explanation.surface: A newspaper headlines a revolt at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'heading' means placed on top. The Sun is a British daily tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise is the moment the sun appears, the start of the day.

clue.text: Order plant

definitions.meaning: the Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the ..., Scotland's chivalric order
a prickly weed with purple flowers, Scotland's emblem

explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's highest order of chivalry is named after its prickly emblem plant.

clue.text: He sells fruit around the outskirts of Deal

indicators.note: around tells us the fruit wraps itself about the other letters

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer edges, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fruit-seller works on the edges of the Kent town of Deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He sells' is the definition, so the answer is a man. Deal is a seaside town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling hawker who goes about selling small goods.

clue.text: Horse carrying Republican guerilla leader in "Evita"?

indicators.note: carrying tells us the leader's name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Juan Peron, the Argentine president in the musical Evita
Che Guevara, the famous Marxist guerrilla, who is also the narrator of Evita

explanation.surface: A horse carries a Republican guerrilla in the musical about Eva Peron.
explanation.walkthrough: Che, the guerrilla, also narrates the musical Evita, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Percheron is a large French breed of draught horse.

clue.text: Part of England under foreign rule — and most of wales, maybe

definitions.text: Part of England under foreign rule

indicators.note: maybe tells us the letters may come out differently, a loose new arrangement
most of tells us to drop the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A region of England was under foreign rule, perhaps most of Wales too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims Wales to WALE, and 'maybe' rearranges AND plus WALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danelaw was the part of England ruled by Danish settlers in the ninth and tenth centuries.

clue.text: Memory loss of men wandering in the continent

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters are set inside the continent's name

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent

indicators.note: wandering means roaming about, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Men lose their memories wandering across a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the continent' must be a specific one, and the four letters needed fit only Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for a partial or total loss of memory.

clue.text: Think again about councillor retained in a legal position

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning

indicators.note: retained in tells us one piece is held within the other, the abbreviation wrapping round the position

parts.note: onside is a legal position in football and rugby, not offside

explanation.surface: Someone ponders a councillor kept on in a legal post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal position' looks like a lawyer's job but is a sporting term: not offside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to think something over a second time and perhaps change one's mind.

clue.text: Silver disposed of by minority? Not at all

indicators.note: disposed of by tells us the silver is got rid of from the word for minority

parts.note: nonage is the legal state of being a minor, under age
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A minority group has sold off its silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of by' removes AG from NONAGE. Nonage is an old legal word for minority, being under age.
explanation.definitionFit: None used adverbially means in no way, as in 'none the wiser'.

clue.text: Faust's tempter? The devil he is!

definitions.meaning: in Marlowe and Goethe the demon who bargains for Faust's soul
this demon is himself a devil, so the exclamation is literally true

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in disbelief about who tempted Faust.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Faust legend the demon who buys the doctor's soul is a servant of Satan, a devil himself.

clue.text: Asians honour one seen in new assembly

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: new assembly tells us the letters are put together afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: An honour is given to someone seen in a new assembly of Asian people.
explanation.walkthrough: Companion of Honour is a British order of merit, abbreviated by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese are the people of China, an Asian nation.

clue.text: It may take pluck to accompany his alfresco singing

definitions.text: It may take pluck to accompany his alfresco singing

parts.words: It may take pluck to accompany his alfresco singing
parts.note: pluck reads as courage but is plucking strings: a lover singing outdoors beneath a window while playing a lute or guitar

explanation.surface: Singing in public outdoors takes some courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenader sings to a beloved at night outside a window, traditionally plucking a guitar.

clue.text: Purchase obtainable from this ugly old woman by the counter

indicators.note: by tells us the second piece sits beside the first, following it

parts.note: an old crow is an unkind term for an ugly old woman
a bar is the counter in a pub

explanation.surface: Someone buys from an ugly old woman standing by a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' is not buying: it means leverage, a grip that gives mechanical advantage, which a lever provides.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is an iron lever, and purchase is the grip or leverage you get with such a tool.

clue.text: Sportsman to confront a ladykiller

parts.note: a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University at sport
to beard someone is to face them boldly

explanation.surface: A sportsman squares up to a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge University sportsman. 'Ladykiller' looks like a charmer; it is the folk-tale villain who murdered his wives.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebeard is the folk-tale husband who killed his successive wives, a literal killer of ladies.

clue.text: Reproof for nurse cavorting in church

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters are placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: cavorting means prancing about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A nurse is rebuked for dancing about in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church' is the Church of England, abbreviated by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure is formal criticism or blame, a reprimand.

clue.text: Simple worker supporting English cricket side

indicators.note: supporting tells us the last piece holds up the others from below in this down entry

parts.note: leg is the on side of the field in cricket, behind the batsman's legs
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A humble worker backs an English cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts ANT beneath E and LEG. Leg side is the half of a cricket field on the batsman's leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant can mean neatly simple, as an elegant solution is one without needless complication.

clue.text: Endless commotion upset people in East Anglia

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
Endless tells us to drop the final letter

parts.note: a fuss is a commotion
folk means people

explanation.surface: An endless fuss upset people living in eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' means turned upside down. East Anglia is the eastern bulge of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is a county forming part of the region, an example of an East Anglian county.

clue.text: Charge some with ancient rusty cars

indicators.note: some tells us only part of the following words is wanted, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone is put in charge of some old rusty cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals letters taken from inside 'ancient rusty': anciENT RUSTy. 'Charge' is a verb here, to give someone responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust is to charge someone with a duty, handing it to their care.

clue.text: A sight better, we hope, after applying this lotion

definitions.text: A sight better, we hope, after applying this lotion

parts.words: A sight better, we hope, after applying this lotion
parts.note: a sight better means much better, but it also hints at improved eyesight after bathing the eyes

explanation.surface: A lotion that should make things much better.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is a lotion for bathing the eyes, though the word also means nonsense.

clue.text: Land survey made by a part-time soldier

definitions.meaning: a register of a landowner's estates with their boundaries
a member of Britain's Territorial Army reserve

explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is an old record of landed property, and also a member of Britain's Territorial Army.

clue.text: By that means beer is brewed in your old container

indicators.note: in tells us the brewed letters are placed inside the old possessive

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: is brewed means the letters are stewed and mixed up

explanation.surface: Beer is brewed in a container that once was yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' merely repeats that the old possessive holds the brew; it adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby is a formal adverb meaning as a result of that, through that action.

clue.text: Indiscreet Parisian of tender years?

parts.note: the French phrase for an unruly child, literally a terrible infant, now used of a tactless upstart

explanation.surface: A young Parisian who says the wrong thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for an embarrassing child is used of anyone whose remarks shock and embarrass.

clue.text: Thus a horse consumed a cereal

indicators.note: consumed tells us the first word swallows the others inside it

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
a horse is a gee or gee-gee, and gee is the spoken name of the letter G

explanation.surface: A horse ate some cereal, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed' puts A and G inside SO. G comes from 'horse' via gee, the nursery word for a horse that is also the letter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy food from palm pith used like a grain in puddings.

clue.text: Remove salt from polluted sea in delta

indicators.note: polluted means fouled or spoiled, so the letters are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: Salt has to be removed from dirty seawater in a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polluted' rearranges the ten letters of SEA IN DELTA.
explanation.definitionFit: To desalinate seawater is to strip out its salt to make it drinkable.

clue.text: He feeds the flames as a novelist

definitions.meaning: a man who shovels coal into a furnace, as on a steam engine or ship
Bram ..., the Irish author of Dracula

explanation.definitionFit: A stoker tends a furnace's fire, and Bram Stoker wrote Dracula.

clue.text: Chesterton's man the day after Grundy's wedding

definitions.meaning: G. K. Chesterton's novel The Man Who Was ... names its hero after a weekday
in the nursery rhyme Solomon Grundy was married on Wednesday and took ill the next day

explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's 1908 novel is titled after this weekday, which also follows Wednesday, Solomon Grundy's wedding day in the nursery rhyme.
